primary_sources.scope: MIT primary course notes: assumptions, incremental marginal comparison, overage/underage, CDF lower quantile; read pages1–7 extracted text. The note also uses the upper-tail complementary ratio, which must not be confused with CDF alpha.

Original 2000 paper abstract, introductory experimental pattern and model definition pp404–406. Supports the specified experiments, not all managers or all sectors. Full experimental/reanalysis replication not performed.

issues.finding: Only demand changes makes80%wrong contradicts earlier correct statement. Keep original; runtime must keep alpha fixed if Cu/Co fixed and recompute Q from changed distribution.
Can forecast or replenish does not categorically exclude model. Uncertainty after forecasting remains; fixed guaranteed emergency is compatible with the article objective.
Symmetric costs imply a median, not exactly50%strictly each side. Original table has .3/.4/.3 around10.
Economic alpha=.8, cycle service=.9 and pooled unit fill=.99 atQ11 are different. Any service or cash redline is a separate constraint.
Larger cost asymmetry changes target quantile under fixed distribution; discrete order quantity can remain unchanged.
Emergency100 is gross cash; underage80 is incremental. Do not double count. Expectedcost230 is not cashmaximum320.
Policy changes may alter demand but do not logically force a change. Re-estimate conditional distribution without manufacturing evidence.
Store news/history verbatim with provenance; do not upgrade broad most errors or individual bias claims to verified facts.
